MAJOR: `Quota.tenantBucket` runs an O(MaxTenantBuckets) eviction scan (up to 10k entries) under the global `q.mu` on every request that introduces a new tenant once at capacity; a flood of distinct `X-Tenant-Id` values turns each admission into a locked 10k-map sweep (latency/DoS amplification). Use a clock-driven janitor or an LRU with O(1) eviction.

`peekJSONTenant` fully reads and buffers (up to 1 MiB) and `json.Unmarshal`s every JSON POST/PUT/PATCH *before* `q.Acquire`, so denied/over-quota requests still pay full body-read + allocation cost, defeating the quota's purpose as the cost control; skip the peek when the header/query already yields a tenant, or peek after admission.

`GET /metrics` is unauthenticated and now exports pool saturation, tenant-bucket counts and denial counters (docs call it "internal"); on any non-loopback `PF_EDP_ADDR` this is free internal-state disclosure. Gate it behind the admin bearer or an explicit opt-in, consistent with `/admin/limits`.

Graceful shutdown drains for `max(WriteTimeout, 30s)` (180s by default), not the AC's 30s; and when `srv.Shutdown` errors the pool is deliberately never closed and the process just exits, leaving in-flight DB work unobserved. Make drain explicit (30s) and log/close the pool deterministically.

Startup now hard-fails on a superuser DSN (default local `postgres`) unless `PF_ALLOW_SUPERUSER_DSN=1`; existing dev/CI environments will stop booting with no in-repo migration note beyond the doc bullet. Call this out in the runbook/rollout plan.
MINOR: `RoleGuard.RecheckLoop` closes the guard on any single error, including transient DB/network blips → up to `RoleRecheckInterval` (5m) of blanket 503s for all non-exempt traffic; require N consecutive failures (or a grace period) before closing, keeping the metric.
`boolean()` silently defaults unrecognized values (`PF_EDP_ENFORCE_LIMITS=maybe` → true); for security switches it should error out rather than guess.

`weakTokens` deny-list is unreachable: every entry is <24 chars and production already rejects <24-char tokens — a 24-char "changeme"-style token passes. Prefer entropy/known-default checks or drop the dead control.
`CheckDBRole` opens a full transaction for a single read-only `pg_roles` query; a plain `QueryRow` on the pool is cheaper and avoids consuming a conn for a tx.

`fail()` passes raw `err.Error()` through for 4xx paths and relies on a narrow regex redaction (`token|secret|...`); SQL text, file paths and DSN fragments still leak to clients. Prefer fixed messages per status.
`artifactUpload` buffers the whole (now 64 MiB) upload in memory per request; with 10 concurrent uploads that is ~640 MiB RSS. Stream to the object store with a checksum writer.
`EnvelopeFallback.fallbackWriter`/`statusWriter` don't implement `Unwrap()` for `http.ResponseController` (and Hijacker/Pusher), which will break `SetWriteDeadline`/hijacking if added later.
NIT: `config/env-flags.json` reformats every pre-existing entry in the same commit, drowning the ~40 new flags in a 400-line diff; keep registry additions mechanical.
`MigrationTimeout <= ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout` is validated, but `PF_EDP_GLOBAL_RPM < PF_EDP_TENANT_RPM` (an incoherent global<tenant config) is accepted silently.
`/metrics` exposes histograms, but the AC says "counters only"; the doc and code agree with each other, so reconcile the AC or the doc.
`Retry-After` for concurrency denials is a hard-coded 1s with no backoff signal; consider deriving it from observed slot occupancy.
SUMMARY: Solid, well-tested guardrail layer: shared pool, request-id/envelope everywhere, injected-clock token buckets, env-validated config and DB-role fail-closed all land close to the AC, in Go per the language rule, with the contract documented.

Top risks: the tenant-bucket eviction scan under a global lock and pre-quota full-body peeking undermine the quota as a cost/DoS control; unauthenticated `/metrics` leaks internals; the shutdown/drain and role-recheck-failure semantics are harsher than the AC implies and will produce avoidable outages.
